data.name: Devkarth
data.gender_notes: Devkarth is used as a male name in Hindu naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: Devkarth is derived from two Sanskrit words: ‘Deva’ meaning ‘God’ and ‘Karth’ meaning ‘work’. This name signifies that the individual is engaged in divine work, serving the higher purpose of the universe. The name Devkarth carries the meaning “God's Work” and is chosen by families in Hindu traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Sanskrit tradition and is also used in Hindi, Sanskrit, Marathi. Parents who choose Devkarth usually hope their child will grow to embody god's work and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.etymology: Devkarth belongs to the Sanskrit linguistic tradition and is used in Hindu naming. Its recorded meaning is “God's Work.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Devkarth total 8, giving a life-path number of 8. Number 8 is linked with Saturn and with the qualities of ambition, resilience and material success.

data.cultural_impact: The name Devkarth is of significant value in Hindu culture, as it reflects a deep connection and dedication to the divine. In Hinduism, following the path of the gods and working towards the betterment of oneself and society is an essential aspect. This name can be seen as an expression of that commitment, encouraging the bearer to live a virtuous life that is in line with the principles of dharma and karma.
data.spiritual_significance: Devkarth carries a strong spiritual significance, as it implies that the individual is not only connected to the divine but is also actively engaged in spiritual practices that contribute to their spiritual growth. The name serves as a constant reminder that one's actions have consequences, not only in this life but also in the next. It encouraging the bearer to choose righteous paths and to strive for inner peace and happiness, as they embark on their spiritual journey towards self-realization and union with the divine.

historical_references.reference:
The Hindu god Devkarttikeya, also known as Devakarth, was the god of knowledge, wisdom, and literature in Hindu mythology. He is considered a son of Lord Shiva and Goddess Parvati. Devakarttikeya is often depicted with a trident, a book, and a peacock feather in his hand.
Reference: Encyclopedia Britannica.
historical_references.time_period: Ancient India (circa 3rd Millennium BCE - 13th Century CE)

historical_references.reference:
Devakarttikeya is mentioned in various Hindu scriptures, including the Agni Purana, the Skanda Purana, and the Mahabharata. In these texts, he is described as the commander-in-chief of the armies of the gods and a great warrior who was instrumental in defeating various demon armies. He is also said to have been the teacher of the celestial sage Vyasa, who authored the Mahabharata and the Puranas.
Reference: Hinduism Today.
historical_references.time_period: Ancient India (circa 4th Century BCE - 13th Century CE)
